record.file_problem: Repository README and file list only; the paper and code were not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports results from Heretic's weight-editing search guided by refusal directions, but does not report the original difference-in-means projection ablation/addition method.
record.gate_note: The main validation table reports minimum refusal rates after a 200-trial Heretic search at four KL budgets, for clean and Bait-and-Recover checkpoints. The key-result table repeats the KL<=0.10 values and is not separately counted. The README also reports utility scores, but these do not measure refusal-direction removal or refusal behavior. Described diagnostics and search choices are not treated as outcome rows.
record.test_reason: Reports refusal rates after Heretic's direction-guided weight-edit search (abliteration) on two released instruct models, clean and defended. This bears directly on V2, using a different, search-based edit rather than the original single difference-in-means ablation.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: Bait-and-Recover raises the lowest refusal rate reachable by a 200-trial Heretic search at low KL while keeping clean-behavior divergence and benchmark changes small. The README also states that, on clean checkpoints, direction editing sharply lowers refusal.
record.recipe_differences: Reports Heretic's automated weight-edit search guided by refusal directions rather than the original difference-in-means residual-stream projection ablation/addition. This is a defense/tool repository, not a reproduction of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported minimum refusal changes with KL budget, checkpoint (clean versus Bait-and-Recover), and model.

fits_no_version.finding: A weight-merged observation-behavior decoupling defense keeps a high refusal floor under adaptive direction-guided editing, with small MMLU-Redux/IFEval changes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The refusal direction measured from activations can be decoupled from the computation that controls refusal, defeating abliteration without loss of utility.

record.peer_reviewed: AACL-IJCNLP 2026 Main (accepted, as stated in README)
record.problems: Only two highlighted models are reported in the README; no uncertainty estimates or prompt/sample counts for the refusal-rate results are stated there. Repository code and paper were not inspected or run.
record.rows_left_out: None of the claim-relevant results reported in the README were left out. The MMLU-Redux and IFEval utility snapshot was not recorded as rows because it evaluates benchmark scores rather than the refusal-direction editing behavior named by the versions.

untested.parts: The difference-in-means direction itself; ablation and addition at all layers; inducing refusal; capability effects of that intervention.
A direct single-direction weight orthogonalization; refusal rates of the unedited models; models beyond Qwen3-8B and Gemma-3-12B-it.
Whether prompt jailbreaks suppress the direction; adversarial training against the ablation.

missing.what: Refusal rates of the unedited clean and defended checkpoints, needed to size the removal.
missing.locator: Not in README; possibly in paper/Bait-and-Recover.pdf or release_artifacts

missing.what: Prompt counts, refusal judge, and the full paper results (more models, ablations).

record.verdict_notes: README only. The tranche is T2 because Heretic is a search over layers, modules, signs and scales, not the original single-direction ablation. Defended checkpoints are deliberately engineered against this attack, so they qualify V2's scope rather than challenge it. V3 links were removed: no jailbreak mechanism was tested and the defense is not training against the ablation.

versions.untested_parts: Difference-in-means direction; projection at every layer and position; adding the direction; effects on general capabilities after that intervention.

The README reports Heretic weight-editing search outcomes, but does not establish that the edit is a direct conversion of the original ablation into a weight edit or that refusal is fully removed in all released models.
Training against the direction's ablation is not tested; the reported defense uses Bait-and-Recover, described as observation-behavior decoupling.
No test of whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or distributed across multiple directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No comparison of refusal training methods or timing to determine whether one removable direction exists.

relation.reason: Its own clean-checkpoint attack results bear on whether a weight edit removes refusal. It does not just use the direction as a tool.

tranche.reason: It reports refusal rates after a direction-guided weight-edit search (Heretic) on clean released models, a different method aimed at V2's question. The defended-checkpoint results add a setting where removal is much weaker.

source_check.notes: The text is the README only. It states no prompt set, n, refusal judge or unedited refusal rates, and it is the code release of arXiv:2609.05794, so don't count the two as separate studies. capability=y refers to MMLU-Redux/IFEval of clean vs defended unattacked models, not edited ones. The pack gave no [lN] ids, so l1-l3 follow the pack's verdict order.

statements.problem: Correct for this study: Gemma-3-12B-it clean 12% (KL<=0.05) and 3% (KL<=0.10) against 83% defended at both. The repo is the code release of arXiv:2609.05794 (the README links it), so it is not independent corroboration of that paper.

statements.correction: Qwen3-8B clean checkpoint; 200-trial Heretic search over per-layer and global direction scopes, attn.o_proj/mlp.down_proj, edit signs, scales and layers ('not a single-layer manual edit'); minimum refusal 36% (KL<=0.05), 11% (<=0.10), 11% (<=0.20), 8% (<=1.0); unedited refusal not stated; rows r1-r4.
statements.problem: Numbers are right (Qwen3-8B clean: 36%/11%/8% at KL<=0.05/0.10/1.0, no unedited baseline). Filing them under single-direction removal misreads the method: the README says the Heretic search spans per-layer and global direction scopes. The cited rows omit r4.
